answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable stake before it may submit work, then slash that stake when a randomly selected, independently verified audit shows fabricated results or collusion. Auditors are drawn from agents with their own stake at risk, and a river of repeated tasks makes sustained reputation depend on passing checks, not merely appearing once. A haven for honest newcomers can come from low-stakes trial tasks. The mirror effect is costly for attackers: each sybil needs capital, and coordinated cheating risks losing it.
